prompt: In a right triangle, $\cos\theta = \dfrac{5}{13}$ where $\theta$ is an acute angle. What is the value of $\sin\theta$? Give your answer as a decimal rounded to the nearest hundredth.
hint: Cosine gives you the adjacent side and the hypotenuse. Find the third side.

hints.text: Cosine gives you the adjacent side and the hypotenuse. Find the third side.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try a $3$-$4$-$5$ triangle: if $\cos\theta = \tfrac{3}{5}$, the third side is $4$, so $\sin\theta = \tfrac{4}{5}$. Sketch the triangle from the ratio, then read the side you need.
Adjacent $= 5$, hypotenuse $= 13$, so the opposite side is $12$.

learningObjective: Find one trig ratio from another using the triangle sides.
explanation: $\cos\theta = \dfrac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}} = \dfrac{5}{13}$, so treat the adjacent side as $5$ and the hypotenuse as $13$.
By the Pythagorean theorem the opposite side is $\sqrt{169 - 25} = 12$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Or use the Pythagorean identity
steps: $\sin\theta = \tfrac{12}{13}$, taking the positive root since $\theta$ is acute.
Sketching the triangle is usually faster and less error-prone, but the identity works when no triangle is described.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: Re-entering 5/13 — the cosine you were given — or forming 5/12 are the two designed misses.
Sketch the triangle: adjacent 5, hypotenuse 13, so the missing opposite is 12 and sine is 12/13. The drawing keeps the three sides in their lanes.
